title: High-dimensional sparse recovery from function samples -- Decoders, guarantees and instance optimality (Theorem 2.8)
author: Moritz Moeller, Sebastian Neumayer, Kateryna Pozharska, Tizian Sommerfeld, Tino Ullrich
work: High-dimensional sparse recovery from function samples -- Decoders, guarantees and instance optimality
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Theorem 2.8 (source0.tex lines 396-403, printed as Theorem 2.8), the paper's sampling-complexity guarantee for function recovery: with at least the number of samples required by the bounded-orthonormal-system sampling bound, the square-root Lasso or orthogonal matching pursuit decoder recovers any f in the weighted A_1-space with an L_q error bounded by a universal constant times the n-term approximation error plus the L_infinity tail, with high probability. The retained complete proof (lines 405-442) is a genuine 38-line argument, not a routine verification: it must transfer the vector level robust null-space-property guarantees to the coefficient level, control the passage from coefficient estimates to L_q function estimates through the A_1 norm of the dictionary, split the error into the n-term approximation part and the off-support part, and interpolate between the endpoint exponents q=2 and q=infinity to obtain the whole range. The residual difficulty is that a probabilistic sampling statement, a deterministic sparse-recovery inequality and a function-space interpolation must be combined with constants tracked uniformly in the sample size; this is research-level high-dimensional approximation theory well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying exercises.
